proofUses.reason: The internal cluster event retains its closed boundary; independent coordinate blocks give the recurrence. A smaller explicit rate covers all radii, and a rational example refutes the stronger stated rate.
Finite Russo differentiation counts every boundary edge once and integrates the sharper density inequality. The critical shell argument retains outward edge multiplicities.

The positive-field range begins at the infinite-cluster probability. Integrating the scalar inequality from that endpoint proves the square-root and finite-mean bounds, conditionally on the displayed differential inequality.

Local Lipschitz regularity permits integration of the assumed almost-everywhere second differential inequality. A field power lower bound yields the density estimate; G192 supplies the percolation inequalities with local Lipschitz regularity.

Finite tori give the two inequalities by closed pivotality and last pivotality in the product space including mark edges. Uniform positive-field convergence passes the combined scalar inequality pointwise and the separate parameter inequalities distributionally, hence almost everywhere.
